title: Idempotent Script Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Python
Scripting
Idempotency
Automation
description: Two side-by-side panels compare a non-idempotent script, which appends the row taxonomy-names.json to a file every time it runs, with an idempotent script, which checks for the row first. Buttons run each script, run both, and reset, so the learner can compare the end state of the two files after repeated runs.

learningObjectives: Differentiate the end state produced by an idempotent script from a non-idempotent one after running each multiple times.
Identify the existence check as the code that makes a script idempotent.
prerequisites: Can read a two-line Python if statement
Has read the definition of idempotent script design

controls.label: Run Non-Idempotent Script
controls.description: Appends another row to the left file on every click

controls.label: Run Idempotent Script
controls.description: Checks for the row first; adds it only if it is missing

controls.label: Run Both
controls.description: Runs both scripts once so their run counts stay equal

controls.label: Reset Both
controls.description: Empties both files and sets both run counters to zero

controls.label: Panel
controls.description: Shows what kind of real script the panel stands for

assumptions: Each file starts empty after Reset Both
The sim opens with each script already run three times
limitations: Models a single row in a single file; real scripts may need to compare more than an exact match

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner applies the same repeated action to two scripts and observes the divergent end states
keyQuestions: On which run do the two files stop matching?
Which line of code is responsible for the difference?
commonMisconceptions: A script that ran without an error left the data in a correct state
Idempotent means the script does nothing
assessmentOpportunities: Describe the check that would make an append-style script safe to run twice
